title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
summary: ESA's Solar Orbiter passed through a large S-shaped fold in the solar wind's magnetic field and measured the charged oxygen and carbon particles inside it. Their composition showed the plasma came from hot magnetic loops on the Sun, released when open and closed field lines reconnected. Waves and turbulence then appear to shape the fold as it travels outward, helping scientists understand how charged particles follow magnetic field lines and improving space weather forecasts.

title: Fastest star in the Milky Way feels the rotation of our central black hole
summary: The Milky Way’s massive black hole is rapidly rotating, and a star in an unprecedentedly close orbit could help measure its spin

title: Webb measures distance to farthest fast radio burst, suggesting origin
summary: Using the Webb telescope, astronomers located the host galaxy of FRB 20240304B, the most distant fast radio burst yet found, and measured its redshift as 2.148. The galaxy turned out to be a small, young dwarf that formed most of its stars quickly. This favours the idea that these brief radio flashes come from magnetars rather than from slow neutron star mergers, and the burst's signal also carried imprints of matter it passed through.

title: Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has imaged NGC 7129, a star-forming nebula about 3,300 light-years away, using infrared light that passes through dust which blocks visible light. Its brightest star, a pre-main-sequence star of 5 to 8 solar masses, is shrinking under gravity and heating up before hydrogen fusion begins. Outflows and radiation from young stars have carved a cavity spanning about 3.5 light-years, compressing gas that may form new stars.

title: Scientists may have found a shortcut to fusion energy
summary: Researchers at Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory have calculated that a fusion reactor might reach ignition more easily if its plasma is heated first and only then made denser, rather than the usual order. This reversed approach could let future reactors become self-sustaining while using much less energy and avoiding problems that make ignition harder. Fusion requires high temperature and density so that nuclei can overcome electrostatic repulsion and fuse.

title: Optical skyrmions can control the motion of magnetic skyrmions
summary: Researchers report that patterns of light called optical skyrmions can be used to steer magnetic skyrmions, which are tiny swirls of magnetisation inside some magnetic materials that act much like particles. Because these swirls are very small and need little energy to move, they could carry information in low-power memory and logic devices. Precise control of their motion has been a major goal, so this approach links light and magnetic fields in a potentially useful way.

title: From spin wave to superconducting circuit: A one-way street for quantum information
summary: Scientists at Argonne National Laboratory and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign have shown a way for information to travel in only one direction, from a spin wave in a magnetic material to a superconducting circuit. Spin is a quantum property of particles that can store and process information. Controlling the direction of this signal flow could help magnetic materials become useful parts of future quantum computers, sensors and secure communication systems.

title: Infrared light overcomes mirror coating obstacle in gravitational wave detector upgrades
summary: Researchers have developed and tested a new locking method for gravitational wave detectors that will advance the discovery of distant black holes and neutron stars colliding.
